stories.title: Arlington Aerospace Supplier Building $45M Addition
stories.excerpt: Circuit Systems Co. Inc. plans to begin construction in November to expand its manufacturing warehouse at 5301 W. Pioneer Parkway. The contract manufacturer makes aerospace bonding jumping cables, bus bars and grounding straps. The expansion is expected to cost $45 million. The company will add 20,980 square feet to its existing 11,880-square-foot facility. The expansion also includes new offices, a conference room, storage and restroom facilities. Circuit Systems products — used in commercial and military aircraft — include parts of the F-22 and F-35 aircraft from Fort Worth-based Lockheed Martin Aeronautics as well as those used in the International Space Station. Those parts provide a safe pathway for electrical currents on aircraft, preventing damage from lightning strikes. The post Arlington Aerospace Supplier Building $45M Addition appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Circuit Systems expanding Arlington facility by 21k SF; $45M investment Nov start
Aerospace supplier serving Lockheed Martin, F-22/F-35 programs; manufacturing expansion signals defense sector strength
New office, storage, restrooms added; signals employer headcount/operational growth in Fort Worth metro
stories.summary: Circuit Systems, a Lockheed Martin aerospace parts supplier in Arlington, is investing $45 million in a manufacturing facility expansion adding 20,980 square feet to its 11,880-square-foot footprint, with construction starting in November. The expansion includes new offices, conference space, and support facilities. The company manufactures electrical bonding and grounding components for commercial and military aircraft including F-22 and F-35 jets.
stories.impact: Defense contractor expansion signals sustained demand in Fort Worth's aerospace cluster and indicates employer headcount growth; multifamily developers should monitor Arlington and surrounding submarkets for rental demand tailwinds tied to contractor and Lockheed Martin staff growth, particularly for workforce housing near defense facilities.

stories.title: 384-Room San Antonio Airport Hotel Trades Hands
stories.excerpt: Hospitality and multifamily investor LXMI Capital acquired the DoubleTree by Hilton San Antonio Airport. The company scored a $36.4 million acquisition loan from Fortress Investment Group. The property at 611 NW Loop 410 had been owned by Presidian Hospitality. Situated at 611 Northwest Loop 410 in San Antonio, Texas, roughly two miles from San Antonio International Airport, the hotel features 384 guest rooms and approximately 14,659 square feet of meeting and event space. Amenities include free self-parking, an outdoor pool, a fitness center, and a complimentary 24/7 airport shuttle service. The 13-story hotel has room rates between $109-$169. Presidian bought the hotel in 2019 and immediately began a $10 million renovation plan. The hotel was built in 1981 as La Mansion del Norte. The post 384-Room San Antonio Airport Hotel Trades Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LXMI Capital acquires 384-room DoubleTree San Antonio Airport for undisclosed price; $36.4M Fortress loan
Hotel trades at $109–$169 nightly; prior owner invested $10M renovation post-2019 purchase
Hospitality-focused investor signals continued appetite for airport-proximate lodging; modest deal size suggests secondary market
stories.summary: LXMI Capital, a hospitality and multifamily investor, acquired the 384-room DoubleTree by Hilton San Antonio Airport from Presidian Hospitality using a $36.4 million construction loan from Fortress Investment Group. The 13-story property, located 2 miles from San Antonio International Airport, features meeting space, free parking, pool, and 24/7 shuttle service. Presidian had purchased the asset in 2019 and completed a $10 million renovation.
stories.impact: Modest deal size and investor composition (hospitality + multifamily specialist) reflects San Antonio's secondary-market status and limited capital intensity for lodging; unlikely to signal broad capital availability for multifamily development, but LXMI's diversification into hospitality suggests hospitality weakness may redirect capital toward residential if airport-hotel cap rates remain compressed.

stories.title: Safeway Opens at 200K-SF Gilbert Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Thompson Thrift celebrated the grand opening of Safeway at The Gilmore, the company’s 35-acre mixed-use development in Gilbert. The 64,000-square-foot Safeway grocery store is located at the northwest corner of Val Vista Drive and Germann Road, just off Loop 202. The Gilmore features approximately 200,000 square feet of grocery, restaurant and retail space and the 300 luxury apartment homes at The Residences at The Gilmore. The Residences at The Gilmore will offer studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom apartment homes with amenities, including a heated swimming pool, 24-hour fitness studio, coworking lounge with private focus rooms, outdoor entertainment kitchen, resident social spaces and a dog park with pet spa. Residents will also balcony and patio options. Thompson Thrift remains highly active across Arizona with several notable developments, including Pointe17 and Refinery at Pointe17 in Phoenix, The Maddox in Buckeye, Stella in San Tan Valley, Southbridge Marketplace in Maricopa, Elliot Tech Center in Mesa, Germann Commerce Center in Queen Creek and more. The post Safeway Opens at 200K-SF Gilbert Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Thompson Thrift opens 64k SF Safeway at The Gilmore; 35-acre mixed-use Gilbert development
300 luxury apartments (studio to 3-bed) at Residences at The Gilmore; amenity-rich positioning
200k SF retail/grocery/restaurant component anchored by Sprouts competitor; grocery-anchored mixed-use trend in Phoenix West Valley
stories.summary: Thompson Thrift celebrated the grand opening of a 64,000-square-foot Safeway at The Gilmore, a 35-acre mixed-use development in Gilbert, Arizona. The center totals approximately 200,000 square feet of retail, restaurant, and grocery space alongside 300 luxury apartment homes (studio to 3-bedroom) with amenities including pool, fitness center, coworking lounge, and dog park. The site sits at Val Vista Drive and Germann Road near Loop 202.
stories.impact: Completed multifamily component at established mixed-use project demonstrates sustained Phoenix West Valley demand and absorption of premium units; the grocery-anchored retail ecosystem validates tenant and resident draw, signaling strong sublease economics and potential for future-phase expansion; developers should assess Gilbert's northeast corridor (Val Vista/Germann) for infill multifamily or retail-residential opportunities given demonstrated leasing velocity.

stories.title: PGIM Sells Delray Beach Assisted Living Community for at Least $140M
stories.excerpt: PGIM Real Estate sold a relatively new assisted living facility in Delray Beach, Fla., for at least $140 million, marking one of the biggest South Florida retirement home sales in recent years. Chevy Chase, Md.-based Artemis Real Estate Partners purchased the 7.2-acre asset, property records show. The 224,951-square-foot community, called The Arbor at Delray, houses 207 apartments at 6595 Morikami Park Road, just west of South Jog Road. The complex includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and a 51,461-square-foot nursing home. The sale breaks down to just under $676,300 per unit, though it’s unclear whether the $140 million figure listed on the deed also includes the operations for the business, which could boost the price tag. PGIM Real Estate, part of insurance giant Prudential Financial, completed the property in 2023. Two years earlier, PGIM-backed Alliance Residential Company purchased the land for $8.2 million and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Dallas-based Comerica Bank, The Real Deal reported. There’s been an uptick in the number of assisted living facilities across Palm Beach County this year as the occupancy rate in Florida neared 90 percent, with monthly rents averaging over $5,000 in the second quarter of 2026, according to data from Colliers. Just last week, Healthpeak Properties bought a 136-unit facility in Boynton Beach for at least $62 million. Representatives for Artemis and PGIM did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: PGIM Real Estate sells The Arbor at Delray assisted-living community; $140M+ price, Artemis acquires
207-unit asset completed 2023; $676k per unit; 224k SF with nursing home and clubhouse
Two-year hold and significant exit valuation; signals strong South Florida senior-housing cap-rate environment and institutional investor appetite
stories.summary: PGIM Real Estate sold The Arbor at Delray, a 207-unit assisted-living community completed in 2023, to Chevy Chase-based Artemis Real Estate Partners for at least $140 million (approximately $676,300 per unit). The 224,951-square-foot property, located at 6595 Morikami Park Road, includes a 35,586-square-foot recreational clubhouse and 51,461-square-foot nursing home. PGIM's development partner Alliance Residential purchased the land for $8.2 million in 2021 and secured a $45.7 million construction loan from Comerica Bank.
stories.impact: Strong exit valuation ($140M+ on $45.7M construction debt plus ~$8M land) reflects robust South Florida senior-housing demand and cap-rate compression, but asset class is healthcare/assisted-living, not market-rate multifamily; relevant for developers evaluating Delray Beach submarkets and mixed-age housing strategies, but limited direct signal for traditional apartments unless demonstrates strong rental-demand fundamentals in broader South Jog Road corridor.

stories.title: Mamdani Invests $8.4M in Business Improvement Districts Citywide
stories.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani is upping the grant funding available to local organizations that promote commerce — though it doesn’t look like much. Mamdani and the New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) is making $8.4 million available to business improvement districts for public art displays, street cleaning, lighting and directories. While $8.4 million might not be the most impressive figure, the administration says it could boost foot traffic for 20,000 businesses in the five boroughs, and is the largest single cash infusion of its kind. “Our administration knows it’s not enough to make it easier to open a small business, you have to make it easier to visit one, too,” Mamdani said in a statement. “That’s why our commitment to small businesses means not only cutting red tape and reducing fines, but investing in the neighborhoods surrounding bodegas, bookshops and restaurants so that New York City is lined with ‘OPEN’ signs year-round.” The grant money has already been awarded, with Brooklyn taking the majority of available funding, or $2.7 million for 32 organizations, while 17 entities in the Bronx received $1.55 million, according to the administration. Manhattan and Queens received similar amounts, while the Bronx saw less funding and Staten Island got the least: $550,000 to only seven organizations. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: NYC Mayor Mamdani allocates $8.4M to Business Improvement Districts citywide; largest single infusion
Grants support public art, street cleaning, lighting, directories; aim to boost foot traffic for 20k businesses
Brooklyn receives majority of funding; signals administrative focus on retail/streetscape vitality across five boroughs
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Department of Small Business Services announced $8.4 million in grant funding for Business Improvement Districts citywide to support public art, street cleaning, lighting, and business directories. The administration stated the grants could boost foot traffic for approximately 20,000 businesses across the five boroughs, marking the largest single cash infusion of its kind. Brooklyn received the majority of funding.
stories.impact: Public investment in streetscape and foot-traffic activation signals focus on retail corridor vitality and small-business retention; while $8.4M is modest relative to NYC's scale, it may reduce retail vacancy risk in ground-floor retail of mixed-use developments and support asset valuations in dense neighborhoods; developers should prioritize ground-floor retail activation and street-level programming to align with municipal priorities and enhance leasing prospects in BID-designated areas.

stories.title: MBA: Multifamily Mortgage Volume Rose 32% in 2025
stories.excerpt: In 2025, 2,530 different multifamily lenders originated a total of $381.8 billion in new mortgages for multifamily properties with five or more units, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) annual report of the multifamily lending market. The total represents a 32% increase over 2024 levels. “Multifamily lending gained significant momentum in 2025, with dollar volume increasing 32% from 2024 as lenders of all sizes remained active across a broad range of capital sources,” said Reggie Booker, MBA’s associate VP of commercial research. “Greater rate stability and clearer pricing expectations helped bring borrowers and lenders back to the market, supporting increased refinancing and acquisition activity throughout the year.” By dollar volume, the greatest share (40% of the total) went to GSEs Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The top five multifamily lenders in 2025 by dollar volume were JPMorgan Chase & Co., Wells Fargo, Walker & Dunlop, Berkadia and CBRE. The post MBA: Multifamily Mortgage Volume Rose 32% in 2025 appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multifamily mortgage volume surged 32% YoY to $381.8B in 2025; 2,530 active lenders
GSEs (Fannie/Freddie) captured 40% of volume; top 5 lenders: JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Walker & Dunlop, Berkadia, CBRE
Rate stability and pricing clarity drove refinancing and acquisition activity throughout 2025
stories.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association reported that multifamily mortgage originations reached $381.8 billion in 2025, a 32% increase over 2024, with 2,530 different lenders active across the market. Government-sponsored enterprises (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac) accounted for 40% of total dollar volume. Greater rate stability and clearer pricing expectations supported increased refinancing and acquisition activity, with JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Walker & Dunlop, Berkadia, and CBRE ranking as the top five lenders by volume.
stories.impact: Strong 32% YoY growth in multifamily lending signals robust capital availability and improved refinancing conditions; GSE dominance (40%) indicates agency appetite remains strong and floors competitive pricing; acquisition activity surge creates opportunities for developers to source construction financing and refinance stabilized assets; however, monitor spreads and floating-rate terms as rate volatility returns—stable pricing window may narrow, affecting new-start underwriting and mezzanine structures.

stories.title: Common Group Unveils Goodyear Retail Center Plans
stories.excerpt: Common Bond Development Group revealed details for its latest commercial development: a premium, grocery-anchored shopping center in the master-planned community of Estrella in Goodyear, Arizona. The project brings together the City of Goodyear, developer Harvard Investments, and anchor tenant Sprouts Farmers Market to establish a new commercial heart for the trade area. Phase one of the development will total approximately 35,224 square feet, featuring a 23,024-square-foot Sprouts Farmers Market, 9,200 square feet of inline retail space, and a 3,000-square-foot standalone pad. A future second phase, situated along the lake, is planned to add 16,000 to 20,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space. The center’s initial design, completed by Suite 6 Architecture + Planning incorporates a maritime theme that reflects its location on Estrella Parkway at North Lake near the Yacht Club of Estrella and the Starpointe Residents’ Club. The project is targeted to break ground in the first quarter of 2027. The post Common Group Unveils Goodyear Retail Center Plans appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Common Bond Development Group unveils Goodyear retail center in Estrella master-plan; Sprouts anchor
Phase 1: 35.2k SF with 23k SF Sprouts, 9.2k inline retail, 3k pad; Phase 2 planned 16–20k SF
Groundbreak Q1 2027; maritime-themed design; signals continued retail density in Goodyear West Valley corridor
stories.summary: Common Bond Development Group revealed plans for a grocery-anchored retail center in Estrella, Goodyear, Arizona, developed in partnership with Harvard Investments and anchored by Sprouts Farmers Market. Phase one totals 35,224 square feet, including a 23,024-square-foot Sprouts, 9,200 square feet of inline retail, and a 3,000-square-foot pad. A future phase will add 16,000 to 20,000 square feet of retail and restaurant space along the lake. Groundbreaking is targeted for Q1 2027.
stories.impact: Retail-anchored mixed-use development in Estrella confirms continued westward population and commercial density migration in Phoenix metro; developers should evaluate nearby multifamily opportunities in Goodyear's retail corridors as retail anchors typically precede or co-locate with residential build-out; master-planned community amenities (yacht club, residents' club, lake) support rental demand for workforce and active-adult housing in the trade area.

stories.title: Developer Plans 297 Housing Units Across From Downtown Brooklyn Macy’s Project
stories.excerpt: Another residential tower might be coming to Downtown Brooklyn, directly across from a major retail makeover project at the former Macy’s. Local developer Shimon Klein has filed plans with the New York City Department of Buildings to bring a trio of 99-unit residential buildings along Fulton Street between Bridge and Lawrence streets. The 99-unit nature of the filing means Klein will likely try to utilize the city’s controversial 485-x tax abatement program, which comes with a construction wage requirement for projects with 100 or more units. Klein’s proposal calls for a 99-unit, 27-story building at 485 Fulton Street. The registered architect is Kao Hwa Lee from Kao Hwa Lee Architects. Neither the architect nor the developer responded to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. If approved, the building at 485 Fulton Street would have between four and eight residential units across the third through 27th floors. There would also be commercial and community facility space, as well as nearly 3,000 square feet of outdoor rooftop space for tenants. There are no further amenity details, but offerings including workout space, communal lounges, and coworking options have become non-negotiables in new residential developments. The other two 99-unit buildings would be built at 147 and 149 Lawrence Street, with similar makeups, according to the filing. The tenants of Klein’s new project would have a plethora of entertainment options in the neighborhood. The building is located across the street from 422 Fulton Street, a former Macy’s department store, which is being renovated into a five-floor retail and entertainment spot called BKX, CO previously reported. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Shimon Klein files 99-unit residential tower at 485 Fulton Street; 27-story building across from Macy's redevelopment
Unit-count structured to avoid 485-x tax abatement wage requirement; commercial/community facility space included
Positioning avoids construction-wage mandate; signals developer cost sensitivity and development economics pressure in Downtown Brooklyn
stories.summary: Local developer Shimon Klein filed plans with the NYC Department of Buildings for a 99-unit residential tower at 485 Fulton Street in Downtown Brooklyn, directly across from a major retail renovation at the former Macy's. The 27-story building will feature residential units on floors 3–27, with commercial and community facility space, plus 3,000 square feet of rooftop amenity area. The 99-unit filing structure suggests Klein intends to utilize the city's 485-x tax abatement program to avoid the construction wage requirement mandated for projects with 100 or more units.
stories.impact: Unit-count ceiling to circumvent 485-x wage requirements signals tight project economics in Downtown Brooklyn and developer caution on labor-cost burden; adjacent Macy's redevelopment retail anchor may support ground-floor retail leasing but indicates prolonged commercial uncertainty; residential approval and delivery timing tied to retail activation will be critical to absorption—monitor site for financing and entitlement delays that often accompany retail-dependent mixed-use projects in challenged secondary CBD corridors.

stories.title: Payments Manager Corpay Cross-Border Relocates to 18K SF at 560 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: An international payment and currency risk management firm is planning a headquarters relocation to Rudin’s 560 Lexington Avenue. Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, which operates under corporate payments company Corpay, has signed an 11-year lease for 17,778 square feet at the Plaza District tower, Commercial Observer has learned. The landlord declined to provide the asking rent, but an April lease inside Rudin’s 22-story tower asked $84 per square foot, according to previous CO reports. Jacob Rosenthal and Kevin Carroll of CBRE represented Corpay, while Rudin was represented in-house by Kevin Daly and a CBRE team of Peter Turchin, Brett Shannon, Eric Deutsch and Lauren Levy. Corpay Cross-Border plans to move from Tishman Speyer‘s 300 Park Avenue into its new, prebuilt office, which occupies the entire 17th floor of 560 Lexington, this fall. Daly, Rudin’s vice president of office leasing, stated that the deal validates recent portfolio investments, which allowed for minimal modifications to meet Corpay’s space requirements. “This allowed us to accommodate their accelerated timeline for move-in, which was a big factor in getting the deal done,” Daly said. Located two blocks from Grand Central Terminal, the 380,000-square-foot office building at the corner of Lexington Avenue and East 50th Street has seen over 91,000 square feet of leasing activity in the last six months, according to Rudin. Recent arrivals include financial firm Marex, hedge fund SummitTX and coworking firm Industrious. Spokespeople for CBRE and Corpay Cross-Border did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Corpay Cross-Border signs 11-year lease; 17,778 SF at Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue; headquarters relocation
Relocating from 300 Park Avenue (Tishman Speyer); move-in fall 2025; asking rent ~$84/SF (Apr market)
International payments/currency-risk firm; prebuilt space with minimal TI; signals Plaza District office demand resilience
stories.summary: Corpay Cross-Border Solutions, an international payments and currency risk management firm, signed an 11-year lease for 17,778 square feet on the entire 17th floor of Rudin's 560 Lexington Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District. The company is relocating from Tishman Speyer's 300 Park Avenue with a planned move-in in fall 2025. The asking rent was approximately $84 per square foot (as of April market), and Rudin's prebuilt space required minimal tenant improvements to meet Corpay's timeline.
stories.impact: Midtown Plaza District office lease of 17.7k SF to financial-services firm signals selective institutional tenant demand outside Midtown South/Hudson Yards; however, fintech/payments processing is lower headcount-per-SF than traditional office, limiting downstream residential demand; lease validates Rudin's asset management and prebuilt strategy but represents localized tenant move rather than net job creation—developers should not assume office leasing strength translates to broad Manhattan multifamily demand without measuring net employment growth in source and destination buildings.

stories.title: John McCullough of Kennedy Wilson Multifamily Development: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Since joining Kennedy Wilson following the firm’s $347 million acquisition of Toll Brothers’ apartment living platform in 2025, John McCullough has been serving as president of the real estate investment company’s multifamily development group, where he oversees every aspect of the firm’s U.S. development business. Kennedy Wilson’s acquisition of Toll Brothers’ platform gave it general partner interests in 18 apartment and student housing properties, with assets under management of $2.2 billion. The firm also purchased a pipeline of 29 development sites in various stages of construction. Toll Brothers’ entire apartment living management team has transitioned over to Kennedy Wilson under the leadership of McCullough, who previously led apartment living operations at Toll Brothers. But McCullough’s real estate path wasn’t always laid out for him, as he started out in the U.S. Navy and then eventually hit his business stride at school in Boston. Commercial Observer caught up with McCullough last month to discuss his entry into real estate, the Toll Brothers acquisition, and his mission at Kennedy Wilson. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: How’d you get started in real estate? John McCullough: I got started in real estate in a roundabout way. I went to the United States Naval Academy for my undergrad, and graduated in 1994, and then served five years in what we would refer to as the surface navy. If I had stayed in the Navy long-term, I would have trained to be the captain of a ship. I served on two large aircraft carriers out in San Diego, and it was a great experience. It was a really good grounding in the fundamentals of leadership I was put into a lot of situations that were incredibly difficult as a 23- or 24-year-old, but I learned a lot from that. bullets: Kennedy Wilson acquired Toll Brothers apartment platform for $347M; $2.2B AUM; John McCullough leads
Acquisition includes GP interests in 18 apartment/student-housing properties; pipeline of 29 development sites
Entire Toll management team transitioned; McCullough now president of multifamily development group
stories.summary: Kennedy Wilson completed its $347 million acquisition of Toll Brothers' apartment living platform, gaining general partner interests in 18 apartment and student housing properties totaling $2.2 billion in assets under management and a pipeline of 29 development sites in various stages of construction. John McCullough, who previously led apartment living operations at Toll Brothers, transitioned to Kennedy Wilson as president of the firm's multifamily development group, overseeing all U.S. development operations. The entire Toll management team moved to Kennedy Wilson under McCullough's leadership.
stories.impact: Strategic acquisition consolidates ~29 development sites under single operator and signals Kennedy Wilson's capital deployment into multifamily development at scale; pipeline concentration may reduce competitive lot availability in markets where Toll was active (particularly Sun Belt/West); monitor Kennedy Wilson's start timeline and capital allocation—large pipeline under single ownership can accelerate or defer deliveries, affecting submarket supply and rental rate pressure in affected metros; merger of management teams may also signal potential site sales or joint-venture activity if capital constraints emerge.
